# Cycle 44 — Visual Design Reviewer

**REVISE.** The LTR Home repair works in both themes. The RTL certification table still shows two apparently empty status rows at its initial edge and midpoint.

## Independent inspection

I opened the accepted preview at port 47851 and candidate at port 47852 in Google Chrome. I compared 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and dark. I inspected Home at the start, middle and end of the table, at the restored position after ordinary and rapid refreshes, and with the document switched to RTL. I opened phone Explorer, tested selected Azure search results from the Blog listing, inspected the Linux disk article’s ordinary table and Azure’s article typography and fenced PowerShell, and opened and dismissed the Home graph on wider layouts. I compared all six table sheets and six context sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-44/`. My own browser captures and geometry are in `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/visual-47851/` and `visual-47852/`.

## Findings

- **Material, RTL.** On the 390px phone at the initial edge, the “In Progress” header occupied x=295–372, while CAISP was at x=−395 to −355. The viewport of the table started at x=18. The dash disappeared too. Both status cells stayed empty at the midpoint; when panned fully the values appeared on the far side of the table from their labels. Tablet and desktop showed the same missed positioning in both themes. The previous site already had this defect. Cycle 44 fixes only its LTR manifestation. The physical left text alignment in the certification cell is a plausible cause. The phone screenshot `visual-47852/390-compare.png` shows the three RTL positions followed by LTR end and refresh states.
- **Minor, phone dividers.** In my 390px Chrome captures, restoring the last column occasionally moved or interrupted a 1px rule under the sticky label relative to its value. All glyphs remained legible. The affected rectangle was limited to the first 77px of the pinned column. This was invisible in the equivalent 900px and 1440px image differences. I would not hold acceptance for this detail.
- **LTR improvement.** The two short values stayed beside their pinned labels while the long credentials row panned, including the 418px phone, 128px tablet and 97px desktop offsets. Normal and double reloads retained the last column in both themes. Before the repair the statuses disappeared during panning and reload returned the row to its start. The ten credential links kept their distinct underlines, rhythm and visible keyboard outlines.
- **Graph and motion.** The 1440px Home graph and opened global view rendered on the first load and subsequent ordinary and rapid refreshes in default Chrome and when WebGL was disabled. In the latter case a 2D canvas showed the links and nodes in their established palette. The tablet graph sat below Home content, the desktop graph in the rail; the phone omitted it. With reduced motion active at first paint the graph had zero height and zero canvases, and toggling the preference removed the active graph after cleanup. Escape returned focus to the wider-layout launcher.
- **Typography, theme and surroundings.** SN Pro status text stayed at 14px and followed the original table baseline. Source Serif 4 prose measured 16.175px, 17.45px and 18px at the three widths. TX-02 code remained 14.5px/22px. Search, the archive’s narrow stacked rows and wide date columns, Explorer and the Linux table retained their original hierarchy and left edges. The page background measured #faf9f5 and #000000. No extra horizontal page width appeared in the tested Home states.
- **Scope and maintainability.** The two short status spans in `content/index.md`, measured offset in `quartz/components/scripts/scrollableTables.inline.ts`, and screen-only sticky declarations in `quartz/styles/custom.scss` are suitably local. The graph renderer and dialog are kept with the graph scripts. The RTL correction belongs with the existing certification cell alignment. These findings are demonstrated behavior, with no separate stylistic preference blocking the cycle.

# Cycle 44 · Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**REVISE.** At the accepted baseline and first build I inspected Home, Blog, the Linux disk article’s table and the Azure Machine Configuration article’s code in live Chrome 158.0.8127.36 at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and pure-black dark. I compared all six paired table sheets and all six context sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-44/`. I tested native Firefox full-page zoom independently.

- The candidate keeps CAISP and the Todo dash beside their row headers in LTR with JavaScript at start, midpoint and end. One reload restored the end positions of 430, 128 and 97px. Rapid double reload restored midpoints of 215, 64 and 49px. The accepted build lost position. The named scroll region and physical right-edge fade still work.
- **Material, directionality.** On all three widths with the root direction set to RTL before load, the short values are outside the visible area or behind the pinned heading at start and midpoint. Both reach the viewport at the far end. The signed positions themselves survive reload. The table still sets physical left text alignment. Separately, Chrome's last link AZ-900 can receive keyboard focus beyond the viewport in RTL. The 390px case puts its outline 352px beyond the scrollport. This also occurs with the accepted build. LTR Tab and Shift+Tab reach all ten links with the entire 2px outline inside the scrollport.
- **Material, static Home.** With JavaScript disabled, the short values scroll away again. At 390px the CAISP text begins 132px before the wrapper at halfway and 347px before it at the end. At 900px and 1440px the sticky row heading covers the values halfway. A stylesheet fallback for the measured inset and logical text alignment belong in the existing Home rule.
- Native Firefox zoom at 100%, 200% and 400% produced 1280, 640 and 320 CSS-pixel viewports. Both values remained readable at all three horizontal positions and in both themes, without page-wide overflow. A separate Chrome 320px reflow check stayed within the viewport.
- The table uses SN Pro 14px. Its status ink has 17.50:1 contrast against the light page and 19.26:1 against black. The focused certificate outline has 13.00:1 and 15.61:1. Article code uses TX-02 at 14.5px. Paragraphs use Source Serif 4. The Linux table retains independent overflow on phones.
- Tested phone Explorer open/Escape, SPA Home to Blog to both articles, keyboard Search, result selection and Escape focus return. Where Graph View is present, Enter focused the dialog Close control, Tab stayed inside, and Escape returned to the opener. The phone and a reduced-motion cold load have zero graph canvases. Toggling reduced motion while the graph was open hid its control, tore down both canvases and moved focus to the site title. Restoring motion brought back one local canvas.
- Maintainability is reasonable within the component: existing table semantics and the scroll region remain available. The missing CSS fallback leaves ordinary visible text dependent on JavaScript. These are reproduced defects, not stylistic preferences.

Primary evidence: the paired browser sheets under `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-44/`, plus my independent `first-access.json`, `47852-access-nojs.json`, `47852-access-native-zoom.json` and `47852-access-motion.json` under `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/`.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# Cycle 44 · CSS and Quartz V5 review

**Decision: REVISE.** Three defects reproduced. The default LTR presentation and ordinary scroll restoration work.

## Evidence and coverage

Independently opened the baseline on port 47851 and first build on 47852 in Google Chrome 158. Reviewed the paired table and surrounding-page sheets under `design-evidence/refresh-repair/first` at 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, in light and pure-black dark themes. The live sweep covered Home, certificate links, status text, the Blog folder, an Azure search with ArrowDown and Escape, Explorer, a nine-row Linux article table, and TX-02 code in the Azure Machine Configuration article via Quartz navigation. Tested full refresh, two rapid reloads, left/mid/right panning, RTL, keyboard focus, CSS zoom, graph dismissal by Close and Escape, and live reduced motion. Two individual tablet LTR samples timed out in the parallel run. Independent Chrome screenshots and the successful light-tablet and dark double-reload runs confirm the ordinary state; neither timeout is counted as a site defect.

## Improvements and maintainability

- Both short statuses stayed beside their row labels in LTR, including while the obtained row panned. The baseline lost the labels' values when the table moved. Ordinary phone refresh restored 430 px; the baseline restored zero. The different range in the supplied phone sheet follows the pointer/viewport setup.
- Reviewed the frozen Home markup, custom SCSS, scrollableTables script and emitted graph bundle. Two status spans, a sticky logical inset, and the row-scoped keyboard exception fit the existing table rule. The measured size accounts for the first cell and the adjacent padding. The observer, cleanup map and scoped Home lookup respect Quartz's nav/render lifecycle. No new stylesheet or theme override. The one per-document pagehide handler avoids a listener per table.
- The graph bundle tracks live mounts, slug and configuration, and invalidates pending work using AbortController. The upstream component still provides its data configuration; the new script owns runtime rendering. After a settled motion preference change the tablet had zero/one local canvases, and Chrome returned focus to the trigger after ordinary dismissal. The phone had no graph. The two reviewed graph inks followed the theme, and article code stayed 14.5 px TX-02. Tables used SN Pro. Blog showed 56 entries and search returned eight options.

## Demonstrated defects

1. **Material — RTL values missing or detached.** At 390 px the first and middle RTL positions had no visible CAISP in either theme. At the other end it appeared about 220 px from the header. At 900 px that last gap was 526 px. The inherited physical left text alignment starts the inline sticky fragment at the far end of its wide cell. Use logical start alignment in the existing table cell rule.
2. **Material — refresh loses the trailing column at fractional scaling.** Chrome at 390 px, DPR 1.25 and 125% CSS zoom reported scrollLeft 508.7999878 and scrollWidth minus clientWidth 508 at native end. It saved 1.0015748; the explicit magnitude-at-most-one guard rejected the saved value and the reload opened at zero. Clamp a finite ratio and retain its direction.
3. **Material — overlapping global graph renderers can throw in Pixi.** On a desktop local graph, held Pixi initialization, opened the global graph, dismissed and reopened it, then released pending work in reverse order. Chrome emitted two uncaught null-read errors in Pixi's batch renderer. The DOM reported the expected local/global canvas count. Evidence in `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/graph-qa/chrome-47852-css-first.json`. Renderer disposal must isolate resources still needed by the surviving graph.

No critical blocker, typography preference, general cascade regression or additional visual change requested.

designDirector.assessment:
## Cycle 44 · REVISE

All three reviewers voted REVISE. The first candidate restored ordinary LTR scrolling and kept the two short status values visible while readers panned the long row. In RTL the values disappeared at the initial and middle positions. Without JavaScript they also scrolled away in LTR. The fractional restoration check discarded a valid native endpoint, and overlapping graph initializations produced uncaught Pixi errors when the first renderer released shared resources. The additional TypeScript diagnostic in the graph test fixture was introduced by this cycle. These material failures outweigh the improvements. Carry forward logical text alignment, a font-relative CSS fallback, handling for fractional endpoints, renderer-local resource disposal and a typed fixture correction. The intermittent single-pixel divider variation was cosmetic.
